concepts.title: Properties of Magnets
concepts.definition: A magnet is an object that attracts magnetic materials; it has two poles where the attraction is strongest and the force is weakest at the middle.
concepts.key_idea: A magnet attracts iron and a few other materials, has two poles, and the magnetic force is strongest at the poles and weakest at the centre.
question_patterns: what are the main properties of a magnet
where is the magnetic force strongest in a bar magnet
which materials does a magnet attract
why does a magnet have two poles
describe how a magnet interacts with iron objects

solution_steps.action: identify the magnet and test object
solution_steps.explain: note the type of magnet (bar, horseshoe) and the material being tested.
bring the magnet near the object and see whether it is attracted, and where the attraction is strongest.
confirm that attraction happens at the poles, is strongest there, and is weakest at the middle of the magnet.

worked_examples.question: Where is the attracting power of a bar magnet strongest and weakest?
worked_examples.solution: The attracting power is strongest at the two ends, called the poles, and weakest at the middle of the bar magnet.
worked_examples.answer: Strongest at the poles, weakest at the middle.

worked_examples.question: A magnet does not attract a wooden pencil but attracts an iron nail. What does this show?
worked_examples.solution: A magnet attracts only magnetic materials like iron, not non-magnetic materials like wood. This shows that magnets selectively attract certain materials.
worked_examples.answer: Magnets attract iron but not wood, showing selective attraction.

exercises.question: List three properties of a magnet.
Why is the middle of a bar magnet unable to pick up many iron pins?

concepts.title: Magnetic and Non-Magnetic Materials
concepts.definition: Materials that are attracted by a magnet are called magnetic materials (like iron, nickel, cobalt), while materials not attracted by a magnet are called non-magnetic materials (like wood, plastic, glass).
concepts.key_idea: Only a few metals such as iron, nickel and cobalt are magnetic; most materials around us are non-magnetic.
question_patterns: classify the given material as magnetic or non-magnetic
name three magnetic materials
is plastic a magnetic material
which metals are attracted by a magnet
how can you test whether a material is magnetic

solution_steps.action: bring a magnet near the material
solution_steps.explain: place a known magnet close to the test material and observe whether there is attraction.
if the material is attracted, it is magnetic; if not, it is non-magnetic.
cross-check: iron, nickel and cobalt are magnetic; wood, plastic, rubber and glass are non-magnetic.

worked_examples.question: Classify iron, copper, wood and nickel as magnetic or non-magnetic.
worked_examples.solution: Iron and nickel are attracted by a magnet, so they are magnetic. Copper and wood are not attracted, so they are non-magnetic.
worked_examples.answer: Iron and nickel are magnetic; copper and wood are non-magnetic.

worked_examples.question: A coin sticks to a magnet but a gold ring does not. What can you conclude?
worked_examples.solution: The coin must contain a magnetic metal such as iron or nickel. Gold is a non-magnetic metal, so the gold ring is not attracted.
worked_examples.answer: The coin contains a magnetic metal; gold is non-magnetic.

exercises.question: Sort the following into magnetic and non-magnetic: iron nail, plastic scale, cobalt coin, glass marble.
Name two metals that are magnetic and two that are non-magnetic.

concepts.title: Poles of a Magnet
concepts.definition: Every magnet has two ends called poles -- a north pole and a south pole; like poles repel each other and unlike poles attract each other.
concepts.key_idea: A magnet always has two poles; if a magnet is cut into pieces, each piece still has both a north and a south pole.
question_patterns: how many poles does a magnet have
what happens when two north poles are brought together
name the two poles of a magnet
what happens when a magnet is cut into two pieces
explain the rule of attraction and repulsion between poles

solution_steps.action: identify the poles being brought together
solution_steps.explain: note whether the two poles facing each other are both north, both south, or one north and one south.
like poles (N-N or S-S) repel each other, while unlike poles (N-S) attract each other.
confirm that the observed push or pull matches the like-repels and unlike-attracts rule.

worked_examples.question: What happens when the north pole of one magnet is brought near the south pole of another?
worked_examples.solution: The north pole and the south pole are unlike poles. Unlike poles attract each other, so the two magnets will pull together and stick.
worked_examples.answer: Unlike poles attract, so the magnets stick together.

worked_examples.question: A bar magnet is cut into two equal pieces. How many poles does each piece have?
worked_examples.solution: Even after cutting, each piece is still a complete magnet with two poles -- a north pole and a south pole. So each piece has two poles.
worked_examples.answer: Each piece has two poles (one north and one south).

exercises.question: State the rule for attraction and repulsion between the poles of two magnets.
Can a magnet have only one pole? Give a reason for your answer.

concepts.title: Finding Directions Using Magnets
concepts.definition: A freely suspended magnet always comes to rest pointing in the north-south direction, which is the principle used to find directions.
concepts.key_idea: Because a magnet aligns itself along the north-south line, it can be used to identify the four main directions.
question_patterns: in which direction does a freely suspended magnet come to rest
how can a magnet help us find directions
why does a suspended bar magnet point north-south
what happens if you disturb a freely suspended magnet
explain how to use a magnet to locate north and south

solution_steps.explain: hang a bar magnet by a thread so it can rotate without obstruction.
wait until the magnet stops moving and settles in a fixed orientation.
confirm that the magnet now points along the north-south line, allowing east and west to be found.

worked_examples.question: A bar magnet is suspended by a thread and allowed to rest. In which direction does it point?
worked_examples.solution: A freely suspended magnet always comes to rest pointing in the north-south direction, with one end toward the geographic north and the other toward the south.
worked_examples.answer: It points in the north-south direction.

worked_examples.question: Once you know north using a suspended magnet, how do you find east and west?
worked_examples.solution: Stand facing the north end of the magnet. Your right hand then points east and your left hand points west, because east and west are perpendicular to the north-south line.
worked_examples.answer: Facing north, the right side is east and the left side is west.

exercises.question: Why can a freely suspended magnet be used to find directions?
Describe the steps to set up a suspended magnet for finding directions.

concepts.title: Earth as a Magnet
concepts.definition: The Earth itself behaves like a giant magnet with magnetic poles near the geographic poles, which is why a freely suspended magnet aligns along the north-south direction.
concepts.key_idea: The Earth's magnetic field exerts a force on a suspended magnet, causing its north-seeking end to point toward the geographic north.
question_patterns: how does the earth behave like a magnet
why does a compass needle point north
where are the earth's magnetic poles located
explain the connection between the earth and a suspended magnet
what causes a magnet to align in the north-south direction

solution_steps.action: recall that the Earth acts as a magnet
solution_steps.explain: understand that the Earth has a magnetic field with two poles near the geographic poles.
the Earth's magnetic field pulls the suspended magnet so that its north-seeking end points toward the geographic north.
confirm that this Earth-magnet interaction is the reason a compass or suspended magnet always settles in the north-south direction.

worked_examples.question: Why does a freely suspended magnet always come to rest in the north-south direction?
worked_examples.solution: The Earth itself behaves like a huge magnet. Its magnetic field acts on the suspended magnet and forces it to align along the north-south line.
worked_examples.answer: The Earth's magnetic field aligns the suspended magnet north-south.

worked_examples.question: Are the Earth's magnetic poles exactly at the geographic poles?
worked_examples.solution: No. The Earth's magnetic north pole is near but not exactly at the geographic North Pole. This small difference is called magnetic declination.
worked_examples.answer: No, the magnetic poles are near but not exactly at the geographic poles.

exercises.question: Explain how the Earth acts like a magnet.
What makes a compass needle settle along the north-south line?

concepts.title: Making a Magnet
concepts.definition: A magnet can be made by stroking a magnetic material like an iron needle repeatedly in one direction with a permanent magnet, or by passing an electric current through it.
concepts.key_idea: Stroking in a single direction with one pole of a magnet aligns the tiny magnetic regions inside the iron, turning it into a magnet.
question_patterns: how can you make a magnet from an iron needle
describe the stroking method of magnetisation
why must the needle be stroked in one direction only
what happens if you stroke a needle in both directions
name another method of making a magnet

solution_steps.explain: choose a piece of iron or steel, such as a needle or a blade, that can be magnetised.
rub one pole of a permanent magnet along the needle from one end to the other, always in the same direction, several times.
test the needle by bringing it near iron filings; if it attracts them, it has become a magnet.

worked_examples.question: Describe how to make a magnet using a bar magnet and an iron needle.
worked_examples.solution: Place the iron needle on a table. Stroke it repeatedly with one pole of a bar magnet, moving in the same direction from one end to the other and lifting the magnet away each time. After several strokes, test the needle with iron filings.
worked_examples.answer: Stroke the needle in one direction with one pole of a bar magnet; it then becomes a magnet.

worked_examples.question: Why should the stroking always be in one direction and not back and forth?
worked_examples.solution: Stroking in one direction aligns the tiny magnetic regions inside the iron in the same direction. Back-and-forth stroking would disturb this alignment and the needle would not become a proper magnet.
worked_examples.answer: One-direction stroking aligns the magnetic regions; back-and-forth does not.

exercises.question: List the steps to magnetise an iron needle by the stroking method.
Why is it important to lift the magnet away before each new stroke?

concepts.title: Magnetic Compass
concepts.definition: A magnetic compass is a device with a small magnetic needle pivoted on a pivot so it can rotate freely; the needle always points along the north-south direction and is used to find directions.
concepts.key_idea: The compass needle is a small magnet that aligns with the Earth's magnetic field, making the compass a reliable direction-finding tool.
question_patterns: what is a magnetic compass
how does a compass help in finding directions
why does the compass needle point north
describe the parts of a magnetic compass
in which direction does the compass needle come to rest

solution_steps.explain: note the magnetic needle, the pivot on which it rests and the marked dial showing directions.
hold the compass level and wait for the needle to stop moving.
confirm that the marked end of the needle points toward geographic north, allowing the other directions to be read from the dial.

worked_examples.question: What is a magnetic compass and how is it used?
worked_examples.solution: A magnetic compass has a small magnetised needle pivoted at its centre so it can rotate freely. The needle always comes to rest pointing north-south, so travellers use it to find directions.
worked_examples.answer: A compass is a pivoted magnetic needle that points north-south to find directions.

worked_examples.question: Why does the compass needle come to rest pointing north-south?
worked_examples.solution: The compass needle is a small magnet. The Earth behaves like a magnet, so its magnetic field forces the needle to align along the north-south direction.
worked_examples.answer: The Earth's magnetic field aligns the compass needle north-south.

exercises.question: Name the main parts of a magnetic compass.
Explain why a compass is useful for sailors and travellers.

concepts.title: Attraction and Repulsion Between Magnets
concepts.definition: Two magnets exert forces on each other: like poles (N-N or S-S) repel or push apart, while unlike poles (N-S) attract or pull together.
concepts.key_idea: The force between two magnets depends on which poles face each other; attraction pulls them together and repulsion pushes them apart.
question_patterns: what happens when two like poles are brought near each other
do unlike poles attract or repel
describe the force between two north poles
how can you show repulsion using two magnets
explain attraction and repulsion with an example

solution_steps.explain: note which poles of the two magnets are pointing toward each other.
like poles repel (push away) and unlike poles attract (pull together).
confirm that the magnets either push apart or pull together exactly as the rule predicts.

worked_examples.question: Two bar magnets are placed with their south poles facing each other. What will happen?
worked_examples.solution: Both facing poles are south poles, which are like poles. Like poles repel each other, so the magnets will push apart.
worked_examples.answer: Like south poles repel, so the magnets push apart.

worked_examples.question: One magnet's north pole faces another magnet's south pole. Describe the result.
worked_examples.solution: The facing poles are unlike poles (north and south). Unlike poles attract each other, so the two magnets will pull together and stick.
worked_examples.answer: Unlike poles attract, so the magnets pull together.

exercises.question: State whether the magnets attract or repel: N facing N, S facing N, S facing S.
Describe an activity to demonstrate repulsion between two magnets.
